title: Cempaka Seri: rethinking the townhouse.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #150 | CEMPAKA SERI, KOTA SERIEMAS
excerpt: Thoughtful interiors and room for greenery put a familiar housing format in a different light.
takeaways: Sean highlights daylight, usable rooms and construction quality.
The surrounding landscape is part of the attraction.
The suitability of the daily commute matters.

sections.heading: The neighbourhood comes first
paragraphs: Sean places Cempaka Seri within the wider Kota Seriemas township. His video notes praise the established infrastructure, including roads, landscape treatments, walking and cycling paths, lakes and recreational spaces. This context matters to the review: the appeal extends beyond the townhouse itself.

sections.heading: Solving familiar townhouse problems
paragraphs: His strongest response is to the design and build quality. The usual concerns he associates with townhouses—dark interiors, awkward structural arrangements and cramped rooms—are addressed here. He also values the balance between buildings and open landscape.

Pokok.Asia's accompanying review describes practical touches such as entrance-level storage, a wide stairway, a balcony facing greenery and windows in the bathrooms. These observations help explain the positive response to the layout.

sections.heading: A home has to fit your geography
paragraphs: The original review favours the project for people working around Sepang rather than making a daily journey to central Kuala Lumpur. It also discusses the pandemic's effect on aviation workers, then a key audience for the development. That is historical context from 2021, not an assessment of today's employment market.

The accompanying article leans toward owner occupation rather than rental investment. It cites RM380,000 for 1,800 square feet at the time; that figure is historical and is not a current asking price.

closing: The useful design question is whether the space works for your actual routine. The useful location question is whether the journey does.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's video notes and the accompanying Pokok.Asia review. Full captions were unavailable. Pricing and pandemic commentary refer to the 2021 coverage.
